text.p: SoundView Financial analyst Gary Helmig said he raised his price target on International Business Machines Corp to $124 from $100, over the next six to 12 months, based on an expanded price/earnings ratio.
-- Helmig said that based on his 1999 earnings estimates, he is looking at IBM's price/earnings ratio to expand to about 15 times 1999 estimates of about $8.28/share.
-- IBM is currently trading at about 14.3 times 1998 earnings estimates.
-- "If you look at comparables, this is not an expensive stock," Helmig said.
-- Helmig said other comparable diversified technology firms, such as General Electric Co and Hewlett-Packard Co, are trading at higher multiples than IBM.
-- He also pointed out that there has been a general multiple expansion in the overall market and added that the current economic outlook is cause for even more optimism.
-- "That sets up a favorable basis for IBM, especially with all this money coming into the market," Helmig said. "There are a lot of legs left here (on this stock)."
